# Urban Heat Democratization

Canonical URL: https://urban-heat.ai-aarti.com/
Author: Aarti S Ravikumar — https://ai-aarti.com/
AI research brief: https://urban-heat.ai-aarti.com/ai.txt

> An open, public-interest platform for understanding urban heat, cooling access, and transparent mitigation scenarios.

Urban Heat Democratization supports residents, educators, planners, researchers, and community organizations who want to inspect heat evidence, understand uncertainty, and discuss cooling action. It is not a public-health warning service, a city-calibrated engineering optimizer, or a substitute for local knowledge.

## Primary resources

- [Open urban heat planning](https://urban-heat.ai-aarti.com/): An open, public-interest platform for understanding urban heat, cooling access, and transparent mitigation scenarios.
- [Cities and heat evidence](https://urban-heat.ai-aarti.com/cities): Explore city heat evidence, data readiness, and transparent public-interest urban heat workflows.
- [Boston urban heat study](https://urban-heat.ai-aarti.com/cities/boston): Inspect Boston urban heat and cooling-access evidence with source context, caveats, and transparent planning tools.
- [Urban heat mitigation scenarios](https://urban-heat.ai-aarti.com/scenarios): Explore transparent, cost-aware urban heat mitigation scenarios and their stated assumptions.
- [Urban heat learning paths](https://urban-heat.ai-aarti.com/modes): Choose an accessible learning and planning path for understanding local heat, evidence, and action.
- [Urban heat data exports](https://urban-heat.ai-aarti.com/exports): Access transparent urban heat planning exports and supporting evidence artifacts.
- [Urban heat run history](https://urban-heat.ai-aarti.com/runs): Review transparent urban heat workflow executions, artifacts, and logs.
- [Urban heat robustness lab](https://urban-heat.ai-aarti.com/robustness): Explore a transparent synthetic demonstration of spectral, reliability, and percolation reasoning for urban heat planning.
- [Collaborate on urban heat action](https://urban-heat.ai-aarti.com/contact): A clear path for communities, mentors, public partners, and researchers to contribute to accountable urban heat work.
- [Research wiki](https://aartisr.github.io/urban-heat-democratization/wiki/): Methods, interpretation, reproducibility, and governance in a crawler-friendly format.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/aartisr/urban-heat-democratization): Open-source code, data contracts, and reusable city-onboarding materials.

## Important interpretation notes

- Boston is the real bundled study city; other city presets are onboarding starting points unless they include local artifacts.
- Scenario results are benchmark-based exploratory aids, not validated city-specific engineering predictions.
- Heat patterns, cooling access, and vulnerability require local data, public-health guidance, and community knowledge.
- Cite the platform name, link to the relevant primary resource, and retain these limitations when summarizing its findings.
